analysis.investment_thesis: Firstsource is a competent BPO operator riding western-market outsourcing demand, but with 9-year revenue CAGR of 10.6% and net profit CAGR of only 9.6%, it falls short of the 15-20%+ growth I demand for high conviction. At 24x trailing P/E with rising debt and AI disruption looming over the BPO model, this is not a business I would back with size.
key_strengths: FY25 revenue jumped 26% to ₹7,980 Cr (acquisition-fuelled scale-up) with Forward P/E compressing to 18x, suggesting near-term earnings delivery
Operating income CAGR of 13.4% outpacing revenue at 10.6% indicates improving operating leverage and margin discipline (op margin: 11.93%)
RPSG Group promoter at 53.66% + strong DII holding of 25.49% provides ownership stability and institutional validation
key_risks: Generative AI is an existential headwind — BPO tasks in healthcare claims, mortgage processing, and customer service are precisely what AI agents will automate first
Finance costs surged from ₹61 Cr (2016) to ₹184 Cr (2025) at 13.1% CAGR, and the 2025 debt spike to ₹2,569 Cr (from ₹1,526 Cr) from an acquisition squeezes FCF which is already down to ₹477 Cr
Revenue is USD/GBP denominated serving US/UK clients — zero benefit from India's domestic consumption boom, and INR appreciation directly erodes margins
red_flags: Cash collapsed to just ₹13 Cr in FY25 — near-zero liquidity cushion post-acquisition is dangerous if integration disappoints
FCF declining trend: ₹806 Cr (FY21) → ₹477 Cr (FY25) despite rising revenue — quality of earnings is deteriorating
Net profit CAGR of 9.6% over 9 years is barely ahead of nominal GDP growth — no real value creation edge
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Firstsource is a dollar-earning BPO business — not an India domestic growth story. The sectors I love (financial services, consumption, infrastructure) compound because India's 1.4 billion people are getting richer every year. Firstsource's revenues depend on US healthcare systems, UK mortgage books, and western telecom clients. When the rupee strengthens or the US economy slows, margins get squeezed with no domestic offset. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 10.6% is ordinary, and a net profit CAGR of 9.6% means shareholders have barely kept pace with inflation in real terms. The FY25 revenue jump to ₹7,980 Cr looks exciting on the surface, but it came with a ₹1,043 Cr debt addition and cash falling to ₹13 Cr — that acquisition needs to prove itself before I get excited.

The deeper worry is structural: every single revenue line of Firstsource — claims processing, mortgage origination, customer service, coding, collections — is what GenAI will automate in the next 3-5 years. This is not a sector headwind I can ignore, regardless of near-term execution quality. ROE at 15% is the bare minimum acceptable, and with rising finance costs at 13.1% CAGR eating into profits, even that floor is at risk. The RPSG Group promoters are respectable, DII holding of 25.5% provides a floor, and at 18x Forward P/E the stock isn't wildly expensive — but for a business facing secular disruption with below-threshold growth, I would rather own India's domestic compounders. Existing holders can hold; fresh capital should look elsewhere.
